newsitem.title: USA: GM would keep 80 pct of Delco/Delphi spinoff.
newsitem.headline: GM would keep 80 pct of Delco/Delphi spinoff.

text.p: General Motors Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Jack Smith said Wednesday the automaker would likely retain about 80 percent of its combined Delco Electronics and Delphi Automotive Systems unit in any future spinoff of the operations.

Smith told reporters after a speech to the Economic Club of Detroit that the company would need to receive several shareholder and government approvals to consolidate the two units before it could finalize plans of a future public offering.
Smith said the amount of ownership in Delphi/Delco that would be offered to the public at a future date "would not be more than 20 percent."

He said one of the possible models for Delphi/Delco's future structure would be Japan's Denso Corp, the former Nippondenso Co Ltd, which is closely tied to Toyota Motor Corp but sells to automakers worldwide.
"What we're talking about is a smart-parts, smart-systems Delphi," Smith said.
Smith added that certain core technologies or components now grouped in the two units may be excluded from the entity that is spun off. He declined to name any specific groups.
Smith did not offer a figure on how much GM expects to save by combining its Delco and Delphi Systems operations. But savings per vehicle could reach into the hundreds of dollars, he said.
GM said last month it planned to merge the two units as part of a restructuring of its Hughes Electronics Corp unit. The merger is tied to the sale of Hughes' defense assets to Raytheon Co.
